title: Avoid repeated hierarchy-index rebuilds during resolved snapshot generation
description:
## Summary
Remove the hidden O(N) hierarchy-index rebuild behind repeated `CreatureDefinition.FindPart` calls in the generation-critical resolved snapshot path.

## Scope
- Thread one `CreaturePartHierarchyIndex` through `ResolvedCreatureSnapshot.Resolve` and `ResolvePartFrameToCreatureSpace`, or use an equally narrow immutable index boundary.
- Include the mesh-asset assembly call site that repeats `FindPart` for resolved mesh parts.
- Preserve the authoritative `CreatureDefinition` model, mutable editor semantics, parent traversal behavior, malformed-definition handling, deterministic ordering, and snapshot output.
- Do not add a mutable cache to `CreatureDefinition` without an explicit invalidation contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A single index is constructed for one resolved generation pass and reused for ancestor traversal and mesh-part source lookup.
- Focused tests prove identical resolved transforms, parent/cycle/missing-parent behavior, and deterministic output before and after the change.
- A benchmark or instrumentation check demonstrates that repeated generation no longer reconstructs the full hierarchy index per ancestor.
- Editor mutation-heavy `FindPart` callers remain correct and are not forced onto stale cached state.

## Validation
Run whole-project .NET compilation before focused runtime tests. Run the nearest snapshot/world-transform tests and record benchmark or allocation evidence. Unity PlayMode validation is required for final generation closure; do not claim it from source inspection.

## Findings
The 2026-09-09 skeleton/animation deep dive confirmed that `CreatureDefinition.FindPart` constructs a fresh `CreaturePartHierarchyIndex` on every call. `ResolvedCreatureSnapshot.Resolve` calls the resolver for every part and each ancestor, creating O(N^2*D)-like repeated work as hierarchy depth grows. Round 21 also found a third generation-critical mesh-asset `FindPart` call site. Existing TSK-0159 covers hierarchy-index element ownership, not rebuild cost. This is a distinct P1 performance mechanism.

## Blockers
Unity execution is unavailable during this reconciliation. No runtime behavior change is claimed until focused tests and Unity validation run.

## Next Step
Design the narrow resolved-pass index parameter and add a regression/benchmark before changing editor lookup semantics.

Please check and make sure all of the audits have been fully ingested and turned into tasks as appropriate"

## Audit corroboration (2026-09-10)
Round 22 `docs/audits/creaturecreator-round22-definitionvalidator-hierarchy-rebuild-2026-09-09.md` confirms the hierarchy-index mechanism is broader than resolved generation: `DefinitionValidator.Validate` rebuilds the index eight times per call, with six `.Parts` loops that do not need an index. Keep this finding under TSK-0192, extending its acceptance criteria to thread one index through validation or use direct `definition.Parts` where no hierarchy lookup is required. Do not create a duplicate hierarchy task.
